properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 18 at 12:02PM ChST until October 20 at 6:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...SUPER TYPHOON CHAMPI MOVING WEST-NORTHWEST AWAY FROM GUAM
COASTAL WATERS...
...A TROPICAL STORM WARNING AND TYPHOON WATCH ARE NO LONGER IN
EFFECT FOR TINIAN AND SAIPAN...

.NEW INFORMATION...
The Tropical Storm Warning and Typhoon Watch for Tinian and Saipan
are cancelled.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides important information and
recommended actions for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota.

Although tropical cyclone watches or warnings are not in effect
for Tinian and Saipan, possible impacts from related hazards are
still a concern.

A Flood Watch is in effect for portions of Guam and the Northern
Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that might
be in effect for your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 11 AM ChST, the center of Super Typhoon Champi (29W) was located
near latitude 13.1N, longitude 143.1E. This was about 115 miles
west-southwest of Guam. Storm motion was west-northwest, 290
degrees, at 14 mph. Storm intensity was 150 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Super Typhoon Champi continues to move west-northwestward as the eye
pulls away from Guam coastal waters, with its outermost rainbands
occasionally crossing the island. Sustained winds hover around or
just below damaging tropical storm-force late this morning, with
occasional Typhoon-force gusts to around 75 mph. Champi's eye, and
the destructive conditions within its compact eyewall, narrowly
missed Guam early this morning, passing just 10 miles south of the
southern tip of the island at around 4:26 AM ChST. The eye remains
compact and very well-defined, with a width of around 5 miles. The
islands of Tinian and Saipan are well outside of the radius of
sustained tropical-storm force conditions, but damaging gusts to 45
mph are still occurring. The Tropical Storm Warning, and Typhoon
Watch, are no longer in effect for Tinian and Saipan.

.PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...
properties.instruction:
Fresh to strong southeast to south-southeast winds with occasional
tropical storm-force gusts look to continue today as Super Typhoon
Champi pulls away. Remain alert as sudden, strong gusts could bring
somewhat dangerous conditions at times, especially with passing
showers. Listen for possible flood advisories or warnings.

properties.areaDesc: Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 18 at 12:00PM ChST until October 19 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 14
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...East and south facing reefs of Tinian and Saipan.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM ChST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized
beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As Super Typhoon Champi continues moving away
from the Marianas, swells from the southeast have diminished enough
for surf to drop below 15 FT and for coastal inundation to no
longer be a concern. However, elevated surf and dangerous rip
currents will continue along east and south facing reefs through
tonight.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. Inexperienced swimmers
should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 18 at 12:00PM ChST until October 19 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18
to 24 feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Guam and Rota.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM ChST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some
critical infrastructure may still be inundated. Some shoreline
erosion will occur. Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening swimming
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...South to southeast swells and elevated wind
waves induced by Super Typhoon Champi to the west-southwest will
continue life-threatening surf and significant coastal flooding at
least through early Monday morning.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.description:

Myakka River At Myakka River State Park affecting Sarasota County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Myakka River at Myakka River State Park.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Park Nature Trail floods. Water approaching
porch steps of cabins.

- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:00 PM EDT Saturday was 7.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue falling to 6.6 feet Tuesday
evening.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 7.0
feet on 09/29/1940.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 800 AM EDT.
